questions.q: How does the embed-versus-reference decision in Cosmos DB Core API compare to the same decision in MongoDB (Lesson 8)?
options: It's the same fundamental tradeoff, since Cosmos DB Core API also stores JSON documents
Cosmos DB does not support embedding data at all
Cosmos DB requires all data to be referenced, never embedded
The tradeoff is completely unrelated to MongoDB's version
questions.explain: Cosmos DB Core API documents are genuinely the same kind of JSON structure, so the embed/reference reasoning from Lesson 8 carries over directly.

questions.q: Why would embedding a product catalog inside every order document be a poor choice?
options: It would duplicate the catalog data across every order and make updates expensive and error-prone
Cosmos DB does not allow nested objects in documents
Product catalogs cannot be stored as JSON
It would violate the mandatory partition key rule
questions.explain: A product catalog referenced by many unrelated orders is a poor embedding candidate for the same reason it would be in MongoDB — duplication and update cost.

questions.q: Why does aligning document design with the partition key matter for Cosmos DB modeling?
options: Keeping data that's typically read together in the same logical partition avoids more expensive cross-partition queries
Partition key alignment has no effect on query cost
It only matters for the MongoDB API, not Core API
Cosmos DB automatically ignores partition boundaries during queries
questions.explain: Cross-partition queries are real and possible but generally cost more RUs than single-partition queries, making partition alignment a genuine modeling factor.

questions.q: What genuinely new factor does Cosmos DB add to the embed/reference decision that MongoDB modeling doesn't have?
options: A literal metered RU cost on every read and write, directly affected by modeling choices
Cosmos DB documents cannot contain nested arrays
Cosmos DB requires a fixed schema for every document
MongoDB has no concept of documents at all
questions.explain: MongoDB's tradeoff is about query complexity and consistency; Cosmos DB adds a real, metered RU cost to the same decision.

questions.q: Why can embedding a large, rarely-needed sub-object into every document be a costly mistake?
options: It inflates the RU cost of every write and read of that document, even for requests that never touch the embedded data
It has no cost impact since RUs only apply to queries with WHERE clauses
Cosmos DB automatically strips unused embedded fields at no cost
It would cause the container's partition key to change automatically
questions.explain: Larger documents cost more RUs per operation regardless of whether the embedded portion is actually needed by that specific request.
